title: Design well, check quality, price for profit

say: Design well, check quality, price for profit.
This is the video for module three of Bead Making and Simple Crafts: design, quality and pricing.
Two necklaces can use the same beads, yet one looks expensive and the other looks random. The difference is design.

say: Use the colour wheel. One colour in light, medium and dark is calm and elegant. Two colours opposite each other, like royal blue with gold, are bold.

panel.heading: Simple design rules
items: Monochromatic calm, complementary bold
60% main, 30% second, 10% accent
One focal bead at the centre front
Build both sides out from the centre
Check colours in daylight first

say: Start with about 60% of the beads in a main colour, 30% in a second colour and 10% in an accent. Equal amounts of two strong colours often fight each other.

say: First, the tug test. Hold the clasp in one hand and the beads near it in the other, and pull firmly. Repeat at the other end. Nothing should move.

panel.heading: Three tests before you sell
items: Tug test at both ends
Drape test: hang it, then lay it curved
Wear test for a week on new materials

say: Second, the drape test. Hang the necklace by the clasp, then lay it on a rolled towel. It should curve smoothly with no stiff parts or gaps.

panel.heading: Three tests before you sell
items: Tug test at both ends
Drape test: hang it, then lay it curved
Wear test for a week on new materials

say: Third, for every new design or material, wear one piece for at least a week. Ifeoma in Onitsha did this and found the gold coating rubbed off in 5 days. She stopped buying that bead before twenty customers were let down.

say: Tick your checklist for every piece, not only big orders. In a WhatsApp world, one broken necklace can be shared with fifty people.

panel.rule: One broken necklace can be shared with fifty people.

say: Do not call a piece gold, real coral, or say it will never break, unless you can prove it.

Say gold-tone, coral-style, and give specific facts. Only say nickel-free or stainless steel when the supplier confirms it in writing. And never make bead jewellery for babies, because small beads are a choking hazard.
Let us cost Kemi's necklace. These naira prices are approximate examples. Always use your own receipts.
First, the unit cost. A pack of 100 crystals for about 2,000 naira is 20 naira per bead.
66 crystals, spacers, wire and findings come to about 2,060 naira in materials.
Labour is your time. She takes 1 hour at her chosen rate of 1,000 naira per hour.
Packaging, a pouch and card, is about 250 naira.
Overheads like transport and data are 10% of materials, about 206 naira.
Her full cost is about 3,516 naira. Any price below that loses money, even if it feels like a sale.
Profit is separate from your labour. Labour pays you for your time. Profit lets the business grow and survive slow months.

say: Many small makers add 30 to 50% for retail. Kemi adds about 40%, about 1,406 naira, and rounds to 5,000 naira retail.

say: Selling below full cost means you pay to work. If a customer's budget is small, offer a simpler design with fewer or cheaper beads.

say: To remember. Use 60-30-10 and a clear focal point. Tug, drape and wear test your work. Name materials honestly. Full cost is materials, labour, packaging and overheads. Add profit on top, and never sell below full cost.
